s001.text: UPSC, twenty twenty-one. General Studies Paper One, ten marks, one hundred and fifty words. Mention the global occurrence of volcanic eruptions in twenty twenty-one. Then give their impact on regional environment. Here's a trap. One famous eruption feels like it belongs in this answer, and it doesn't.

s002.text: Read what it asks. Mention means list, briefly. Impact means say what each eruption did. So there are two jobs. Where did they happen? And what did they do to each region?

s003.text: Start with the where. NOAA's database lists seven significant eruptions for twenty twenty-one. Three in the Americas, two in Europe, one in Africa, one in Asia. That is NOAA's filter, not a count of every eruption.

s004.text: But now the trap. Hunga Tonga is not on that list. It erupted in January twenty twenty-two. Tonga is the famous one, so it sneaks into answers. Leave it out.

s005.text: So how big was twenty twenty-one? None passed four on the explosivity scale. La Palma put out one point eight million tonnes of sulphur dioxide. That is about a tenth of Pinatubo. So the damage stayed regional.

s006.text: Regional is the word to build on. Each eruption hit a place in its own way. Ash and water in the Caribbean. Houses and power in Central Africa. Air in Europe. Reefs in the Pacific.

s007.text: Now we write. One hundred and fifty words, about seven minutes. Open with NOAA's seven, and say the effect was regional, not global.

s008.text: Section one is the where. Three in the Americas, two in Europe, one each in Africa and Asia. Then one line that shows you know the trap. Tonga is twenty twenty-two.

s009.text: Section two is the impact, one region at a time, each with a figure. St Vincent: sixteen thousand evacuated, water and power lost. Nyiragongo: five thousand houses. La Palma: eighty-five days and twelve square kilometres of lava. Its plume reached Africa and the Caribbean. And a pumice raft drifted thirteen hundred kilometres to Okinawa's reefs.

s010.text: End with the scale. La Palma's gas was a tenth of Pinatubo's. So no global cooling followed. The harm was regional.

s011.text: Now the easy answer beside it. It adds Tonga and a global cooling. It gives a total count nobody can source. It lists eruptions but not their impact. It says the plume stayed on the island. Both took seven minutes. Only one did both jobs.

s012.text: Here is the payoff. The same frame answers its cousins. Twenty twenty asked about the Circum-Pacific Zone. Twenty nineteen asked about phreatic eruptions. Learn it once: where, then what it did.
